title: PAP Therapy Equipment Records Standard: Open Device Records per Patient
content:
# Open Device Records per Patient — PAP Therapy Equipment

**Standard.** A patient may hold at most 2 PAP Therapy Equipment device records that are open — a record is open in any status other than returned, cancelled or replaced. Of those, at most one is billed to coverage and at most one is a self-pay device. A Travel CPAP System (E0601) is always self-pay. No second self-pay order is opened while another self-pay device record of the patient is in status order received.

**Evidence.** Whether an earlier self-pay record stands in status order received is read from the patient's device records as the system holds them; the patient's own account does not settle it. The check concerns the same patient and is made before the new order is opened; a new order is always a separate device record.

## The limit in a table

| Open records the patient already holds | A new coverage-billed order | A new self-pay order |
|---|---|---|
| none | within the limit | within the limit |
| one coverage-billed | beyond the one coverage-billed record | within the limit |
| one self-pay | within the limit | beyond the one self-pay record |
| one coverage-billed and one self-pay | beyond the limit of 2 | beyond the limit of 2 |

A returned, cancelled or replaced record is not open and does not count toward the limit.

## Points of judgement

- **Is a Travel CPAP System (E0601) ever the coverage-billed record?** No. It is always the self-pay device of the patient.
- **What does the order-received rule add?** A self-pay order is not opened while another self-pay device record of the same patient is still in status order received.

**Example (hypothetical records).** A patient holds an Auto-Adjusting CPAP System (E0601) in active rental billed to coverage and a self-pay Travel CPAP System (E0601) that is patient-owned. Both records are open, so the patient holds 2 open records and no further PAP Therapy Equipment record is opened. If the Travel CPAP System (E0601) record were returned, it would no longer count.
